answers.rationale: Jonah repeatedly prioritizes a no-fee window for solo travel. When a later segment cannot yet be seated, the appropriate handling is to preserve the window preference as a request and revisit it when selection opens. The only included outbound window should therefore be assigned now.

His consistent hierarchy is free window first, aisle as the fallback, and not a closer-front middle seat merely for location. With no standard window available, 16C is the better of the two aisle fallbacks because it is farther forward, while the reservation should be watched for a standard window release.

For a solo itinerary Jonah chooses a free window where available and retains that preference for segments whose maps are not yet open. Assigning 25F now and submitting a window request plus a check-in reminder for the regional segment best follows that pattern.

The default solo-seat preference is an included window rather than a more-forward aisle or a middle. Between the two available standard windows, 24A is one row farther forward than 25F, consistent with his preference for better location after seat type is satisfied.
